subject: Model provenance & release traceability (RFI) — follow-ups and build plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@datatrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael O'Neill <m.oneill@datatrust.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model provenance and release traceability - RFI clarifications

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the initial RFI packet. A couple of follow-ups from our security and SRE teams that would help us close the compliance review: 

1) You reference a model "manifest" — can you confirm the exact fields included (commit hash, source license, upstream weights URL, build environment, quantization artifacts)? Do you publish SHA256 or similar checksums for the artifacts?

2) How does Redwood handle a model update where the upstream license changes (e.g., from permissive to copyleft)? What is the customer-visible workflow for pinning vs allowing automatic rollforward?

3) We need to understand your notification/attestation mechanism when you push catalog updates. Is there an API/webhook we can subscribe to, and do you provide a signed artifact or timestamped audit record?

4) For air-gapped/private deployments (on-prem), do you provide a packaged SBOM and an optional offline attestation bundle?

If you can answer these in detail and attach a small sample manifest, that will speed our procurement loop.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Vendor Security
DataTrust Inc.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@datatrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model provenance and release traceability - RFI clarifications

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below and I've attached a representative manifest and the Excel RFI we filled out for your records. If you want a one-hour walkthrough of how the manifest is generated we can schedule a demo.

1) Manifest fields and checksums
- Canonical fields we include in the model manifest: model_id (catalog id), version, upstream_source (URL or repo), source_commit (git SHA), weights_artifact_url, weights_sha256, license (SPDX), training_data_summary (high-level), build_env (container image + hash), quantization_profile (if applied), recommended_pin_level (recommended pinned variant for stability), and provenance_notes (free text).
- We always publish weights_sha256 and manifest_sha256. For each published release we store both the artifact checksum and the manifest checksum in our internal audit log and include the manifest_sha256 in the release metadata visible in the Console.

2) License change workflow (upstream changes)
- When upstream metadata changes (including license):
  * In Hosted: we create a new catalog entry (new version) and mark prior versions as deprecated only after internal risk assessment. We do not auto-upgrade pinned customer variants. Customers who rely on pinned versions continue to see the same digest unless they opt into the newer version.
  * In Dedicated/Private: we publish the new manifest to the customer-specific catalog and emit an update_notice (see #3). Pinning: customers can set a catalog policy to pin major/minor/patch or to allow auto-rollforward for non-licensing/security-only changes.
- If license changes introduce incompatibility (e.g., adding copyleft obligations), we surface a hard block in the Console and require an explicit customer acknowledgement.

3) Notifications & attestations
- We provide:
  * An updates webhook: POSTs a signed JSON payload (payload includes manifest_sha256, model_id, version, timestamp, and change_type).
  * Audit records are timestamped and stored with HMAC-signed entries and optionally exportable as a signed bundle (PKCS#7) for customers.
  * For customers requiring additional evidence, we can provide a notarized attestation (time-stamped and signed) for specific releases under an enterprise support agreement.

4) On-prem / air-gapped bundles
- We ship an offline bundle containing: the model weights (tar), manifest.json, manifest.sha256, build container image tarball, and a generated SBOM (spdx or CycloneDX). For attestations in air-gapped sites we include a signed attestation file and instructions for customers to verify signatures with Redwood's public key.

I've put more operational details in the attached manifest sample (model-catalog-manifest-sample.json) and the completed spreadsheet. Priyom and Rishi are copied for any technical follow-ups.

Next steps: if you confirm the scope of the attestation and any format preferences (SPDX vs CycloneDX; webhook vs S3 notifications), we will produce a final package and an optional DocuSign attestation for procurement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships (Sales)
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0132

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model provenance and release traceability - RFI clarifications (technical notes)

Vanessa / Priyom — adding technical clarifications for Samantha's team so they can pass to SRE: 

- Manifest signing: we sign manifests with an ephemeral GPG key rotated monthly; manifest signatures are included in the signed bundle and we publish the corresponding public key id + rotation history in the Console.
- Digest stability: weights_sha256 always maps to the *exact* artifact in object store. When we repackage (e.g., different quantization), we create a new artifact with a new sha256 and the manifest references both the original upstream sha and the new artifact sha.
- Automated compatibility checks: for each candidate update we run a small regression suite (prompt set) that checks token-level drift and major metric regressions. If regressions exceed thresholds we mark the update as "quality regression" and block auto-rollforward.
- Canary & rollback: updates route through a canary policy (10% traffic by default on Hosted). If any runtime exceptions or latency regressions occur we auto-rollback and emit an incident with root-cause link.

I'll prepare a short appendix on the regression-test thresholds and can share our synthetic prompt set example for auditing.

—Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@datatrust.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael O'Neill <m.oneill@datatrust.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 09:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model provenance and release traceability - RFI clarifications

Vanessa, Rishi — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of quick clarifications: 

- For manifests signed with the ephemeral GPG key, do you publish the rotation log? We need chain-of-trust for audits.
- Can you confirm the webhook payload is HMAC-signed and includes the manifest_sha256 and a human-readable change_type (e.g., license_change, security_patch, performance_tune)?
- For the offline bundle, will the SBOM be generated in SPDX by default? Our procurement prefers SPDX 2.2.

If those are yes, we can accept the RFI with the conditions noted and move to contracting. I can also share the exact DocuSign template we prefer.

Thanks — Samantha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@datatrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model provenance and release traceability - RFI clarifications (final package)

Samantha — short answers: yes / yes / yes. Details and attachments below; final RFI spreadsheet attached and a sample manifest included in the bundle.

- Rotation log: published in Console under Catalog > Keys with rotation timestamps and key fingerprints; we can export the log as a signed file for audits.
- Webhook: HMAC-SHA256 signed payloads; payload fields include model_id, version, manifest_sha256, change_type (license_change|security_patch|perf_tune|dep_update), and timestamp. Example schema included in the manifest sample.
- SBOM format: default SPDX 2.2, CycloneDX available on request.

I have attached: DT_RFI_20280515_Redwood_Response.xlsx and model-catalog-manifest-sample.json. I've also initiated a DocuSign envelope for the attestation template (link included above). If you want, we can run a short call tomorrow to walk legal/security through the attestation flow.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this.
